name: Retrograde nailing approach to the humeral shaft
corridor: Posterior triceps-splitting window to an entry point just proximal to the olecranon fossa for retrograde humeral nailing

positioning.text: Position prone or lateral with the arm over a support and the elbow flexed so the posterior distal humerus is presented.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the medial and lateral supracondylar ridges, the tip of the olecranon, and the posterior humeral shaft.

incision.text: Make an 8 to 10 cm straight dorsal incision proximally from the tip of the olecranon.

superficial_interval.text: Split the triceps tendon longitudinally and separate the edges with right-angle retractors.

deep_interval.text: Expose bone just proximal to the olecranon fossa, extending about 25 mm proximally from the fossa edge, palpating the medial and lateral columns to center the entry and protecting the elbow joint capsule.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, triceps tendon and muscle, and the posterior supracondylar humerus above the olecranon fossa.

structures_at_risk.text: The ulnar nerve medially and the triceps mechanism are at risk, and a poorly placed or low entry can create a supracondylar stress riser.

danger_zones.text: The supracondylar entry region is the danger zone: an eccentric or distal entry risks iatrogenic supracondylar fracture, and the ulnar nerve lies just medial.

retraction_hazards.text: Protect the ulnar nerve medially and the elbow capsule during preparation of the entry.

exposure.text: Exposes the posterior supracondylar humerus for the retrograde entry point.

limitations.text: The narrow entry corridor above the olecranon fossa and the risk of supracondylar fracture limit nail diameter and mandate a well-centered entry.

indications.text: Indicated to establish the entry point for retrograde intramedullary nailing of humeral shaft fractures.

closure.text: Repair the split triceps tendon and posterior fascia in layers, place a drain if needed, and close skin.

complications.text: Complications include iatrogenic supracondylar fracture, ulnar nerve injury, triceps weakness, and elbow stiffness.

procedure_applications.condition: A humeral shaft fracture is stabilized with a retrograde intramedullary nail

questions.question: Where is the retrograde humeral nail entry point?
questions.answer: Just proximal to the olecranon fossa, centered between the medial and lateral columns.
